links.outcome: Independent (non-AI) colonoscopy quality of CADe-trained vs conventionally trained endoscopists
links.effect: AI-trained endoscopists, performing without AI, had higher ADR (35.5% vs 30.3%; +5.3%, 95% CI 2.9–7.6) and SDR (12.5% vs 7.1%; +5.4%, 95% CI 3.8–7.0); similar CIR.
links.quote: AI-enhanced training improved ADR by 5.3% and SDR by 5.4% (95% CI: 2.9–7.6%, and 3.8–7.0%, respectively) in high-power analysis (98.5–100%).

links.outcome: Unaided post-training adenoma and sessile lesion detection rates
links.effect: During subsequent colonoscopies without AI, AI-trained endoscopists had higher ADR by 5.3% (95% CI: 2.9–7.6%) and SDR by 5.4% (95% CI: 3.8–7.0%).
links.quote: AI-enhanced training improved ADR by 5.3% and SDR by 5.4% (95% CI: 2.9–7.6%, and 3.8–7.0%, respectively) in high-power analysis (98.5–100%).

links.outcome: adenoma and sessile lesion detection rate
links.effect: The AI-trained group had a significantly improved adenoma detection rate by 5.3% and sessile lesion detection rate by 5.4%.
links.quote: AI-trained group had also a significantly improved adenoma detection rate (ADR) by 5.3% (95% CI: 2.9-7.6%) and sessile lesion detection rate (SDR) by 5.4% (95% CI: 3.8-7.0%).
